summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted the day after discharge following an allogeneic stem cell transplant for CML in myeloblastic crisis, presenting with severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and worsening abdominal pain. She had not taken her immunosuppressive medications, including tacrolimus, due to confusion at home. Imaging revealed pancolitis and later new ascites. Colonoscopy showed no infection or graft-versus-host disease. Tacrolimus levels were initially high, and dose reduction led to improvement in symptoms and resolution of ascites. She gradually resumed oral intake, remained stable, and was discharged with a revised immunosuppressive regimen including mycophenolate and prednisone. Thrombocytopenia persisted but was stable, likely related to medication effects.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
